Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The two umpires make their way out to the middle. South African players are in a huddle and then they spread out to take their respective field positions. Will Young and Devon Conway are the two openers for New Zealand. Lungi Ngidi to start proceedings with the ball. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

With 304 runs on the board, South Africa have set a daunting target for New Zealand. The pitch still looks good for batting, but it won’t be an easy chase. Can the Kiwis rise to the challenge, or will South Africa’s bowlers defend this total? We are heading into the second innings. Stay tuned for the chase!

Matthew Breetzke is up for a chat and he admits that his record-breaking debut innings hasn’t fully sunk in yet, though he feels exhausted and wants to take in the moment. He acknowledges that batting was tricky early on, with the wicket being a bit tacky and O’Rourke extracting movement with the new ball. Breetzke focused on spending time at the crease before growing in confidence and eventually enjoying his innings. Looking ahead, he hopes South Africa can strike early with the new ball to put New Zealand under pressure and see how the game unfolds.

At the other end, Mulder played a crucial supporting role, notching up 64 off 60 balls, ensuring South Africa breached the 300-run mark. His knock ended in the penultimate over, falling to O’Rourke, but his contribution had already bolstered the total. For New Zealand, Matt Henry was the standout bowler, returning figures of 2/59 from his 10 overs. O’Rourke also picked up two wickets, while Bracewell chipped in with one, but overall, the bowlers struggled to contain the Proteas' late surge.

After winning the toss, New Zealand elected to bowl first, looking to make early inroads. While Matthew Breetzke started cautiously, Temba Bavuma took the initiative in the powerplay, scoring 20 off 23 balls before O’Rourke found his glove, sending him back early. The Kiwi spinners tightened the screws, slowing down the run rate and forcing South Africa into a rebuilding phase. However, Breetzke and Wiaan Mulder showed great composure, grinding through the middle overs before shifting gears. Their 131-run stand for the fourth wicket was a game-changing moment, with Breetzke stamping his authority on the game.

South Africa walk out with 304 runs in 50 overs after been asked to bat first by Mitchell Santner, thanks to the brilliant record breaking innings from Matthew Breetzke, becoming the first players to score 150 on an ODI Debut!

Commentary.Commentary: Right then! All the pre-match formalities conclude and the players and the umpires walk out and take the stage for the start of the 2nd ODI. It is the pair of Temba Bavuma and Matthew Breetzke opening the batting for South Africa. Matt Henry will start the bowling attack for New Zealand. Let's Play!
The Match Officials and the players walk out in a straight line and take the field for the National Anthems. It is the National Anthem of South Africa first, followed by that of New Zealand.

Aamir Sohail and Bazid Khan analyze the pitch conditions in Lahore, highlighting its usual batting-friendly nature with assistance for spinners. However, they note that pacers could find some movement early on due to the weather and grass cover. They expect conditions to become more favorable for batting as the match progresses, making it a typical Gaddafi Stadium surface. While bowlers may have some help under the lights, they emphasize that batters are likely to dominate the game.

South Africa captain Temba Bavuma expresses confidence in the new faces joining the squad, seeing it as an opportunity for them to showcase their skills at the highest level. With a busy cricket schedule ahead, he emphasizes the importance of making the most of available resources. Bavuma acknowledges the excitement of integrating fresh talent into the team and how they adapt to the setup. Although South Africa would have preferred to bowl first, he notes that there could be some early swing but remains focused on posting a strong total to stay in control of the game

Mitch Santner calls it right at the toss and chooses to bowl first. Says that the wicket looks tacky and it is a quick turnaround. Adds that it was about recovery yesterday but today we will look to see what we can do. Informs that Rachin Ravindra goes out obviously and Devon Conway comes in. Mentions that it looks like a good pitch and there is a touch of grass there. Will look to do something early with the ball with some early movement, he concluded.
